one_month_reasoning: No Synopsys earnings in the window: Q4 FY26 results are expected in early-to-mid December 2026, after 2026-10-31. Scheduled or likely events inside the window: (1) analysts finishing their post-Investor-Day target raises (BofA to $600, KeyBanc to $605) and moving FY27 estimates up from the $17.81 consensus toward the $19.04-19.12 guide; (2) the start of the ~$1B buyback 'over the coming months' (about 1% of a ~$94B market cap); (3) Cadence Q3 2026 results in late October, a sector read-across that could move SNPS by mid-single digits either way; (4) macro and semiconductor-sentiment prints. Short-horizon regularities pull in opposite directions. Drift after a guidance surprise is positive: the FY27 EPS guide beat consensus by ~7% and estimate revisions are still coming through. Against that, the stock rose ~18% in two sessions (415.09 on 9/29 to 490.54 on 10/1) after a September low of $367.70 close, so part of that gain could reverse. Net: median slightly above spot (~$493), with sigma ~12% for the month, a bit below annual 45%/3.5 = 12.9% because no company print falls in the window, roughly symmetric in log terms.

fair_value.method: Blend of 24x FY28E non-GAAP EPS of $23.0 (=$552, 50%), a 3.6% FCF yield on FY28E FCF/share of $19.7 (=$547, 30%), and 29x SBC-burdened FY28E EPS of $18.45 (=$535, 20%). The FY28 figures are built from the Investor Day FY27 guide ($19.08 EPS, $3.1B FCF) and the mid-20s EPS CAGR framework, haircut to ~20% growth.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28E non-GAAP EPS $23.0 x 24x NTM P/E (value as of Oct 2027, when FY28 is the forward year)

inputs_detail.derivation: $19.08 x 1.205. The framework calls for a mid-20s% EPS CAGR FY26E-FY30E from $15.07 (about $36-37 by FY30). FY27 alone is +26.6%, so I haircut FY28 to ~20.5% to allow for slippage and the end of the Ansys cost-synergy tailwind.

SNPS trades at 25.7x the FY27 guide ($490.54/$19.08). CDNS trades at ~43x its 2026 guide ($350.73/$8.10) with 19% revenue growth versus SNPS ~15%. I keep a discount to CDNS for ~$10.0B gross debt (~$6.4B net), a GAAP/non-GAAP gap of ~$5/share SBC plus amortization, and the history of weakness in the IP segment. 24x is a bit below today's forward multiple: the multiple usually compresses a little as growth is rolled forward one year.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28E FCF $3.72B / 189M diluted shares = $19.7/share, valued at a 3.6% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: $3.1B x 1.20. The framework calls for mid-20s% FCF growth; I haircut it to 20%, as with EPS.

The FY27 guide is 190-192M and 191.6M were outstanding on 2026-08-24. The ~$1B buyback (about 2M shares at ~$500) and the policy of returning up to 50% of FCF offset SBC dilution, for a net ~1% drift down.
At $490.54 x 191M shares (~$93.7B), FY27 FCF of $3.1B is a 3.3% yield. I use a slightly higher 3.6% to account for net debt of ~$6.4B ($10.04B debt less $3.61B cash at 7/31/26).

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: SBC-burdened P/E: FY28E non-GAAP EPS $23.0 less after-tax SBC $4.55 = $18.45 x 29x

inputs_detail.derivation: From the Investor Day GAAP-to-non-GAAP reconciliation
Shows the size of the non-GAAP add-backs (SBC plus Ansys amortization)
$970M x 1.08 growth = ~$1.05B, x (1-18% non-GAAP tax rate), / 189M shares

On SBC-burdened earnings, a mid-20s% EPS growth framework and a peer (CDNS) above 40x non-GAAP 2026 EPS support a high-20s multiple. This method is mainly a cross-check that P/E on non-GAAP EPS is not flattering the value.

bear.story: FY27 guide proves aggressive. EDA and IP growth fade after the AI capex peak; agentic AI (including GPT-Synopsys-style tools) erodes seat-based pricing; China export controls tighten, or the Ansys/simulation segment grows only mid-single digits. FY28 EPS of ~$20.5 at ~18x gives ~$370, back near the September 2026 lows.

base.story: Synopsys hits FY27 guidance (~$11.15B revenue, ~$19.1 EPS, $3.1B FCF) and guides FY28 to ~20% EPS growth. Deleveraging and the $1B buyback continue. The market holds ~24x NTM EPS of ~$23, giving ~$545-550.

bull.story: AI design complexity, the AWS $1B+ IP and EDA deal, Factory 2 royalties and GPT-Synopsys consumption revenue push growth above the mid-teens framework. FY28 EPS reaches ~$24 and the multiple re-rates toward CDNS at ~29x, giving ~$700.

thesis_break_reason: $375 is ~19.7x the FY27 non-GAAP EPS guide, below where the stock traded before the Investor Day re-rating (365-415 in September 2026). A move there after the guide would most likely mean the market had stopped believing the FY27/FY30 framework: a Q4 FY26 miss or FY27 guide cut in December, a sharp IP or Ansys slowdown, a new US export-control hit to EDA sales to China, or clear evidence that AI agents compress EDA pricing. Ordinary volatility alone should not take the stock there.

reasoning: Sources are primary documents. The Q3 FY26 8-K and 10-Q show revenue of $2.477B (+42% y/y with Ansys), non-GAAP EPS of $3.91, EDA software +8.5% on a 16% comparison and guided to accelerate to double digits, and Design IP back to +11% after a y/y decline in Q2. Backlog is $10.9B with ~49% due in 12 months; debt is $10.04B against cash of $3.61B; 191.6M shares are outstanding. FY26 guidance is $9.715B revenue, $15.07 EPS and ~$2.6B FCF. The key new information is the 2026-09-30 Investor Day: FY27 revenue $11.10-11.20B (+15%) and non-GAAP EPS $19.04-19.12 against consensus of $10.81B and $17.81 (Reuters); ~44% non-GAAP margin; $3.1B FCF; a framework of mid-teens revenue and mid-20s EPS/FCF CAGR to FY30 with a ~50% margin; a ~$1B buyback; plus the OpenAI GPT-Synopsys revenue share and an AWS deal worth over $1B. The footnotes that recaps skip: GAAP EPS is only $8.16-8.61 and SBC is ~$970M (~$5/share), so the non-GAAP P/E flatters. The stock re-rated from $415 to $490.54 in two sessions and now sits at ~25.7x the FY27 guide. Valuing 12 months out on FY28E EPS of ~$23 (the framework haircut to ~20% growth) at ~24x, cross-checked with an FCF yield and an SBC-burdened P/E, gives a fair value of ~$547 (+11.5%). The scenario-weighted mean is ~$532. I set the median at ~$517, below fair value, because guidance-driven re-ratings partly reverse often enough to matter, the stock had a 45% realized vol year, and the bear case (AI pricing, China, IP) is plausible. The distribution is roughly lognormal with ~38% vol, slightly below realized because the big guidance uncertainty has now been resolved. I trimmed the far right tail: above $860 would need more than 35x earnings for a $94B company. P(>=$392) ~0.77 and P(>=$736) ~0.15. Research limits: the Benzinga transcript and SEC direct downloads were blocked, so the transcript was read via Motley Fool. Twelve Data analyst estimates and statistics needed a higher plan, so consensus came from Reuters. The BofA and KeyBanc targets come from a search-result summary only.
